correctness.rationale: The transform and normalization follow directly from the verified Brion exponential-simplex identity. Lagrange interpolation yields the zero at all complete reciprocal nodes. The exact imaginary Hessian on the real-zero tangent plane has determinant equal to minus the positive barycentric-weight product divided by a square; thus its signature is (1,1) for every node. The real-analytic implicit-function theorem and Morse lemma give precisely two transversely crossing real-analytic curves. Affine invariance follows by substitution. Exact checks cover 120 weight sets; independent moment-series and high-precision branch checks validate normalization and local slopes. Tests are not used as proofs.

value.rationale: The Fourier-zero set of a 3D aperture is generically a curve. The theorem classifies every completely phase-aligned reciprocal node in an infinite natural lattice as an ordinary double intersection, determines the two tangent directions directly from arithmetic Vandermonde weights, and extends the result to every affine tetrahedron. This is a natural geometric invariant of the diffraction zero set and more than a selected example, normalization check or unmotivated finite computation.
